tier_reason: README benchmarks kernels 1-19 against Intel MKL (kernel 0 in the same binary); code is public (repo .c files plus kernel headers), compiler GCC 7.3.0, flags in Makefile (-O0 -march=skylake-avx512 -fopenmp) and CPU Xeon W-2255 are all stated. Results are given only as plots; the text claims 'comparable to / faster than Intel MKL'.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: GCC 7.3.0, Ubuntu 18.04.5; Makefile CFLAGS: -O0 -march=skylake-avx512 -w -lpthread -fopenmp; linked against oneMKL 2021.1 beta (mkl_sequential, ILP64)
corrections.caveats: Tutorial-style. The win over MKL is stated as 'comparable to / faster than', shown only in plots (hosted on cs.ucr.edu, not readable here), on one CPU (Xeon W-2255) against a oneMKL 2021.1 beta. The project's own kernels are built at -O0 (they are intrinsics/inline asm, so -O0 matters less); MKL is the prebuilt sequential library. Kernel sources are linked from cs.ucr.edu. Baseline is MKL, not oneDNN. Last commit Feb 2022 (>3 years).

notes: Claim matches the README wording; I could not open the plot images (cs.ucr.edu blocked by proxy), so the size of the win is unverified. Makefile read: -O0 on own kernels is unusual but handicaps the project, not the baseline. Last commit 2022-02-03 is >3 years old, so abandoned.

tier_reason: ad-benchmarks repo has public per-library benchmark code (xad/, cppad/, adept/, autodiff/, src/) and states GCC 13.3, -O3 -mavx2 -mfma, Intel Xeon Platinum 8488C, Ubuntu 24.04; the open-source XAD tape mode beats CppAD, Adept 2 and autodiff on all four kernels. The XAD-Codegen column needs the commercially licensed xad-codegen, so that part cannot be reproduced from public code.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Open-source XAD tape mode (gradient time) vs Adept 2 / CppAD: Heston MC 40 ms vs 91 / 268 ms; SABR 8.4 ms vs 19 / 32 ms (autodiff 38 ms); XVA CVA 2.6 s vs 7.1 / 8.0 s; LIBOR swaption 1.00 s vs 1.15 / 4.57 s. The page says 'fastest tape library on every benchmark, by margins of ~1.1x (LIBOR vs Adept) up to 2.3x (Heston vs Adept)'. The commercial XAD-Codegen backend is 2x-5x faster than tape mode (Heston 21 ms, SABR 4.9 ms, XVA 0.57 s, LIBOR 0.31 s). Adjoint is ~70x faster than finite differences on LIBOR (161 inputs).
corrections.caveats: The benchmark repo (1 commit, 5 stars, MIT, (c) 2026 Xcelerit Computing Ltd) belongs to the vendor that sells XAD enterprise support and xad-codegen. The headline numbers are XAD-Codegen, a commercially licensed add-on that is not part of AGPL XAD; the open tape mode's margin is only ~1.1x-2.3x over Adept. Baselines are AD libraries (CppAD, Adept 2, autodiff), not oneDNN/XNNPACK/Eigen tensor. autodiff completed only SABR (forward dual mode). AGPL-3.0 is copyleft.

notes: The numbers match the ad-benchmarks README. The record attributed XAD-Codegen numbers (commercial add-on) to the AGPL library, and its SABR 'competitors 8.4-38 ms' counted XAD's own tape time as a competitor; claimed_speedup is rewritten to lead with the open tape mode. Consider recording a shortcoming: vendor-run benchmark, and the headline backend is closed and commercial.

tier_reason: Numbers come from the author's own arXiv preprint (no peer-review venue shown) and the author's ADBenchmark repo. The paper states GCC10, -O3 -march=native, C++17, on a Google Cloud VM with an unnamed 'Intel Xeon Processor' (8 cores). The CPU model is missing, so it is not A, and first-party partial methodology is C, not B.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: GCC10, C++17, -O3 -march=native (per arXiv 2102.03681); ADBenchmark README says it was tested on macOS Catalina with GCC10
corrections.hardware: Google Cloud VM, Ubuntu 18.04.1, 'Intel Xeon Processor', 8 cores (model not stated)
corrections.claimed_speedup: Paper abstract: '2-10 times faster than Adept and 2-19 times faster than Stan across various test cases'; e.g. sum: Adept ~10x and Stan ~15x slower; normal log-PDF: Adept ~9x, Stan ~19x slower; Bayesian linear regression: 8.6x vs Stan and 10x vs Adept at largest N. README: 'over orders of magnitude improvement' (not supported by the paper's 2-19x).
corrections.caveats: First-party benchmarks (author's arXiv preprint, no peer-review venue found, plus the author's ADBenchmark repo). CPU model not stated (an unnamed GCP Xeon VM). README's 'orders of magnitude' claim overstates the paper's 2-19x. Baselines are AD libraries (Adept, Stan Math, ADOL-C, CppAD, Sacado), not the category baselines. Last commit Sept 2023.

notes: The paper does give compiler and flags (GCC10, -O3 -march=native) but no CPU model, and it is the author's own unrefereed preprint, so B becomes C. Benchmark code is public at JamesYang007/ADBenchmark. Metadata (MIT, 122 stars, last commit 2023-09-27, stale) confirmed.
